comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Implementation Regulations and currently linked pre-2027 module chart were freshly retrieved on 8 October 2026. The adopted general structure remains first-year major 60 EC, second-year major 60 EC, minor 30 EC, third-year major 15 EC and Design Synthesis Exercise 15 EC: 180. All 22 previously verified course/module components and their weights are retained unchanged. The 2022–2023 chart is the still-linked applicable pre-September-2027 structure; the September 2027 redesign is excluded from this 2026 entrant reconstruction. Wind-tunnel testing is embedded in Aerodynamics 7 EC, aerospace AI is embedded in Test, Analysis and Simulation 8 EC, and zero-credit reporting/language training does not add credits. The current public Dutch and English programme pages advertise English or Dutch–English and the Dutch page explicitly mentions a bilingual track. Normalized metadata therefore includes ENG and retains NLD; the raw NLD offering remains unchanged. This fresh content qualifies the earlier audit English-only proposal. The generic current instruction options do not establish a different 2026 curriculum, a new formal specialization, or retroactive bilingual-track applicability for the selected entrant. No future curricular units are imported.

programmes.label: Bachelor Aerospace Engineering at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: Aerospace Engineering is a tightly sequenced professional engineering degree. Its compulsory spine combines calculus, differential equations, probability, physics, engineering mechanics, materials and structures, aerospace design and construction, aerodynamics with wind-tunnel testing, structural and vibration analysis, flight and orbital mechanics, propulsion and power, signals and control, numerical modelling, aerospace systems engineering and production, flight dynamics and flight testing, and a 15-EC aerospace Design Synthesis Exercise. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming, numerical methods, linear systems, statistics, AI, robotics, sustainability and general product-design courses. It has no equivalent progression in classical mechanics, aerospace materials and structures, fluid mechanics and aerodynamics, propulsion, orbital mechanics, aircraft stability and flight dynamics, aerospace production, wind-tunnel and flight-test practice, or integrated aircraft/spacecraft design. The available quantitative and computational courses can support an engineering-adjacent liberal-arts pathway, but cannot form a defensible Aerospace Engineering comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-2027 Implementation Regulations confirm the complete 180-EC structure: a 60-EC first-year major, 60-EC second-year major, 30-EC minor, 15-EC third-year major and 15-EC Design Synthesis Exercise. The official pre-2027 curriculum chart accounts for those credits course by course. Year one develops aerospace orientation and engineering drawing, introduction to aerospace engineering, materials and structures, statics and dynamics, two calculus courses, physics, linear algebra, Python scientific computing and a 9-EC aerospace design-and-construction module. Year two advances system design, subsonic and supersonic aerodynamics with wind-tunnel testing, structural and vibrational analysis, differential equations, probability and statistics, test/analysis/simulation with aerospace AI, flight and orbital mechanics, propulsion and power, aerospace signals and control, and numerical analysis and computational modelling. Year three combines a 30-EC minor with systems engineering, aerospace design and production, flight dynamics and simulation with flight testing, and the 15-EC Design Synthesis Exercise.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics add programming, AI and computational applications. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design offers team design, quantitative modelling, fabrication and prototyping; ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design add energy and wind-related sustainability contexts. These are meaningful adjacent courses, but the workbook contains no university physics sequence for engineers, statics-and-dynamics sequence, mechanics of materials, aerospace materials, structural analysis, vibration engineering, fluid mechanics, subsonic or supersonic aerodynamics, wind-tunnel laboratory, thermodynamics and propulsion, flight mechanics, orbital mechanics, aircraft stability and flight dynamics, aerospace telecommunications and instrumentation, flight-test laboratory, aerospace manufacturing and production, or integrated aircraft and spacecraft systems design. DISMATH312 covers mathematical representations of linear systems rather than the target's full aerospace signals, control and flight-dynamics formation; DISDATA312 covers robot kinematics and motion planning rather than aircraft dynamics or aerospace control; and BENENTR111 is general consumer-product development rather than load-bearing aerospace design and certification practice. UCR also lacks a 15-EC capstone equivalent to AE3200 in which the complete aerospace design process synthesises these technical disciplines. The target's defining engineering-science, experimental and design sequence therefore remains overwhelmingly unmatched.
